description: Execution-level races and restart recovery, not planner-only cases. input.scenario selects a reference-executor setup: folder-delete-concurrent-upload inserts an unseen F/new.md after listing; folder-delete-unsupported explicitly declares unsupported atomic empty-only removal; folder-delete-default-unsupported omits the capability and its delete operation throws; folder-delete-runtime-failure declares support but its delete operation fails; folder-delete-unsupported-child-revision-race changes F/a.md after listing before its conditional deletion. new-file-create-race and new-folder-create-race occupy a planned creation path after listing. conflict-copy-restart runs one overlapping edit with losing edit time 1000, injects a crash at input.crashAfter, restarts with durable metadata and completes sync. folder-delete-deferred initially syncs F/a.md, removes local F, then syncs with unsupported capability to preserve empty remote F and create one pending notice. input.event mutates that durable state and syncs again: restart-pending restarts before display; restart-acknowledged acknowledges durably then restarts; new-child creates F/new.md; changed-child restores a recorded F/a.md baseline then changes its remote revision before a fresh plan; ignored-child adds F/keep.pdf; new-empty-subfolder adds F/New; unchanged-subfolders uses an initially synced F/Sub/a.md instead and preserves F/Sub then F, followed by restart; local-recreation recreates local F then deletes it again after one sync; local-recreation-remote-missing removes remote F and recreates local F before the next listing; remote-disappearance removes remote F; identity-replacement replaces remote F and F/a.md with new identities; identity-replacement-restart injects an INITIAL remote file deletion failure, retaining F/a.md record/base while F is preserved, replaces ONLY the parent folder identity (child id/version/bytes unchanged), then injects a remote child read failure after the replacement folder-record transaction; observe old descendant record/base retired before restarting and retrying the child download, counting both operational failures (errors 2). multi-drive uses two linked drives with independent notices, recreates F, removes remote F on the second drive, then syncs the first and second drives; supported removes the capability limitation; failed-listing fails the remote listing. before-preserve-save and after-preserve-save inject on the INITIAL preservation transaction, before it commits or immediately after commit before display, respectively; preserve-save-failure fails that initial transaction; ack-save-failure fails acknowledgement; local-recreation-preflight-restart recreates local F, removes remote F, then crashes after the all-drive recreation transaction before planning. For crash/save events, restart and retry successfully, except ack-save-failure which is observed before acknowledgement is retried. folder-delete-local-recreation-race recreates local F after planning but before its initial preserve action; that action must skip. errors counts all injected operational failures, excluding deliberate crashes; notices counts distinct durable notice lifecycles ever created, not displays or current pending rows. repeatActions counts folder preserve/delete/create actions on one extra unchanged sync after restart. pendingNotices and acknowledgedNotices count durable notice states; activeNotices excludes retired lifecycles. Existing entries and failed-action records must remain intact. Runners must execute and observe these setups, not synthesize expected results; keep separate adapter/persistence tests.
